description: Figure 4 is a single line plot titled “Hidden State Mean” that illustrates mean absolute hidden-state values across network layers for three conditions (before gating, after gating, and a baseline). The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0 to 23 with labeled ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Abs Mean,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 to a little above 4 (with labeled ticks at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4). Three dashed lines are shown without markers: a blue dashed line (“hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71”) starts near 0 at layer 0, rises to around 0.2–0.3 in early layers, stays around a few tenths through mid layers, then increases sharply after about layer 18, reaching roughly 2.6 around layer 21 and ending above 4 (around 4.3) at the final layer. An orange dashed line (“hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05”) stays close to 0 throughout, beginning near 0 at layer 0 and ending around 0.1–0.15 by the last layer with a gentle upward drift. A green dashed line (“hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04”) similarly remains near 0 across layers, starting near 0 and gradually increasing to roughly 0.1–0.15 by the final layer.
